item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
135
ABPZ20 KNHC 230520
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Tue Sep 22 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, about 200 miles offshore of southern Mexico, and on Tropical
Storm Odalys, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of
Baja California.

Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (Former TD 15-E):
Showers and thunderstorms associated with the remnants of Tropical
Depression Fifteen-E, located a few hundred miles south-southeast
the Big Island of Hawaii, have become better organized.
Environmental conditions remain conducive for development, and a
tropical depression could form tonight or Wednesday while the system
moves slowly west-northwestward. Heavy rains associated with this
system are forecast to spread over the southeastern Hawaiian Islands
starting on Wednesday and continuing through Saturday, possibly
resulting in life-threatening flash flooding and mudslides for
portions of the Big Island and Maui. Interests in the Hawaiian
Islands should continue to monitor the progress of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

South of the Gulf of Tehuantepec:
An area of low pressure is expected to form in a couple of days to
the south of the Gulf of Tehuantepec. Afterwards, environmental
conditions should be favorable for gradual development, and a
tropical depression is likely to form late this week or this weekend
as the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward,
parallel to the coast of southern and southwestern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

...ODALYS STRENGTHENS INTO A HURRICANE...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.9N 128.4W
ABOUT 1295 MI...2085 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...75 MPH...120 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...ENE OR 65 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...989 MB...29.21 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Odalys was located 
near latitude 15.9 North, longitude 128.4 West. Odalys is moving 
toward the east-northeast near 9 mph (15 km/h). An eastward to 
east-northeastward motion at a slightly slower speed is expected 
through the next couple of days, followed by a gradual turn toward 
the northeast then north later this week.
 
Maximum sustained winds have increased to near 75 mph (120 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Additional strengthening is expected during the 
next day or two, followed by a weakening trend late this week.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 10 miles (20 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 989 mb (29.21 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly

item.title: Hurricane Odalys Forecast Discussion Number 13
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Wed Sep 23 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 230841
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Odalys Discussion Number  13
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP162026
200 AM PDT Wed Sep 23 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that Odalys has recovered from the 
earlier dry air intrusion. Deep convection has developed over the 
low-level center, with a convective shield that has cold cloud tops 
near -80 C. In addition, a recent WSF-M microwave pass revealed a 
nearly closed low-level convective ring and a developing eye 
feature. A subjective Dvorak intensity estimate from TAFB has 
increased to T4.0/65 kt, and objective intensity estimates from 
UW-CIMSS range between 55 and 68 kt. Based on these estimates and 
the improved structural organization in the microwave data, the 
initial intensity is set at 65 kt, making Odalys a hurricane.
 
The initial motion is estimated to be east-northeastward, or 065/8 
kt. This general motion is expected to continue in the short term as 
Odalys is steered by the flow between a mid- to upper-level trough 
moving into the eastern Pacific and a strong ridge located over 
central Mexico. A turn toward the northeast and then north is 
forecast in a couple of days. Beyond day 3, the steering pattern 
becomes increasingly complex, and potential interaction with 
Hurricane Polo will likely complicate the future track of Odalys. 
The updated NHC track forecast is near the previous advisory, and 
lies near the previous the HCCA and GDMI track aids.
 
Vertical wind shear is forecast to begin relaxing as Odalys 
traverses warm sea surface temperatures, which should allow for 
steady strengthening over the next 24 to 36 hours. By 48 to 72 
hours, wind shear is forecast to increase once again, SSTs will 
cool, and Odalys may begin to experience upper-level outflow from 
Hurricane Polo. At the same time, the cyclone will move into a drier 
mid-level environment, which should induce a weakening trend. The 
official NHC intensity forecast shows a slightly higher peak 
intensity, and is closest to the HCCA and GDMI intensity aids. 
Toward the end of the forecast period, model-simulated infrared 
satellite imagery indicates that Odalys will succumb to a drier 
environment. As the system becomes devoid of organized deep 
convection, it is expected to degenerate into a post-tropical 
cyclone, which is now shown in the latest NHC forecast at day 5.

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Polo Advisory Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
300 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026
 
...OUTER RAINBANDS OF POLO BEGINNING TO REACH THE COAST OF
SOUTHWESTERN MEXICO..
 
 
SUMMARY OF 300 AM CST...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.0N 101.4W
ABOUT 185 MI...300 KM S OF ZIHUATANEJO MEXICO
ABOUT 335 MI...540 KM SE OF MANZANILLO MEXICO
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...155 MPH...250 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...N OR 360 DEGREES AT 2 MPH...4 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...918 MB...27.11 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
None.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* Tecpan de Galeana to Punta San Telmo
 
A Tropical Storm Watch is in effect for...
* West of Punta San Telmo to Playa Perula
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are 
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within 12 
hours.
 
A Tropical Storm Watch means that tropical storm conditions are
possible within the watch area, generally within 48 hours.
 
Interests elsewhere along the southwestern Mexico coast should
continue to monitor the progress of this system as additional
watches and warnings could be necessary later today.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM CST (0900 UTC), the eye of Hurricane Polo was located near 
latitude 15.0 North, longitude 101.4 West. Polo is moving toward the 
north near 2 mph (4 km/h). A sharp turn to the northwest is expected 
to begin later today followed by a general west-northwestward motion 
later this week and over the weekend. On the forecast track, the 
core of Polo is expected to be near the coast of southwestern Mexico 
during the next day or two, although it is forecast to remain 
offshore.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 155 mph (250 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Polo is a category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson
Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in intensity are expected, but
Polo is expected to remain a very powerful major hurricane during
the next few days.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 105 miles
(165 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 918 mb (27.11 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Polo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDEP2 and WMO header WTPZ42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected within the warning
area along the coast of Mexico later today. Tropical storm
conditions are possible within the watch area along the coast of
Mexico on Thursday.
 
RAINFALL: Polo is expected to produce rainfall totals of 3 to 6
inches, with isolated maximum totals up to 8 inches across coastal
portions of the Mexican states of Guerrero and Michoacán through
Thursday. This rainfall may produce life-threatening flooding and
mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain. Rainfall of 2 to 4
inches is possible in coastal portions of Oaxaca, Colima, and
Jalisco through Thursday.
 
For a complete depiction of forecast rainfall associated with Polo,
please see the National Weather Service Storm Total Rainfall Graphic
available at hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep2.shtml?rainqpf
 
SURF:  Swells generated by Polo are expected to affect portions of
the coast of southwestern Mexico during the next few days. These
swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf, rip current
conditions, and coastal flooding. Please consult products from
your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 600 AM CST.
Next complete advisory at 900 AM CST.
 
$$
Forecaster Cangialosi

item.title: Hurricane Polo Forecast Discussion Number 11
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026 
000
WTPZ42 KNHC 230834
TCDEP2
 
Hurricane Polo Discussion Number  11
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP172026
300 AM CST Wed Sep 23 2026
 
Satellite images indicate that Polo remains a powerful major
hurricane. The cyclone continues to maintain a distinct, circular,
and clear eye. However, the convection in the eyewall is not quite
as intense as it had been over the past 24 hours. Although there
have not been any recent microwave images available, there are
still signs in geostationary satellite data that the system has a
double eyewall structure. The initial intensity is set at 135 kt,
which is in line with the latest satellite intensity estimates.
The far northern bands are brushing up against the southwestern
coast of Mexico, and ASCAT data show winds to tropical storm force
just off the coast.
 
The cyclone has moved little over the past several hours, however,
a building mid-level ridge over Mexico and the south-central U.S.
should cause Polo to turn northwestward or west-northwestward later
today. This motion should take the center of the hurricane just off
the coast of southwestern Mexico through Thursday. Even though the
intense core of Polo should stay offshore, outer rainbands are
likely to spread across southwestern Mexico during the next day or
so, producing areas of heavy rain and tropical-storm-force winds.
Polo should pass well south of the Baja California Peninsula Friday
and Saturday, and then likely turn northward when it reaches the
western periphery of the ridge. Little change was made to the 
previous track forecast, and this prediction is near a blend of the 
HCCA, GDMI, and TVCA aids.
 
Fluctuations in strength seems likely over the next day or so, due 
to internal dynamics, while the major hurricane remains in favorable 
environmental conditions. However, a gradual weakening trend is 
expected after that time due to an increase in easterly vertical 
wind shear and slightly drier air. Nonetheless, Polo is forecast to 
remain a powerful hurricane during the next several days. The NHC 
intensity forecast lies generally near the middle of the guidance 
envelope.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Heavy rainfall associated with Polo will impact coastal portions
of southwest Mexico through Thursday. This rainfall may produce
life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of
steep terrain.
 
2. A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for portions of 
southwestern Mexico, and a Tropical Storm Watch is in effect 
westward to Playa Perula. Interests in these areas should closely 
monitor updates to the forecast.
